subject: Chemistry
unit: Unit XVII — Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
title: Reactions of α-Hydrogens: Aldol, Claisen-Schmidt, Cannizzaro, & Iodoform
topics: Enolate Anion Resonance Stabilization & α-Hydrogen Acidity (pK_a ≈ 20)
4.1 Aldol Condensation Mechanism (dil. NaOH) yielding α,β-Unsaturated Carbonyls (Crotonaldehyde)
Claisen-Schmidt Reaction (Crossed Aldol: Benzaldehyde + Acetaldehyde ──► Cinnamaldehyde)
4.2 Cannizzaro Reaction (Self-Redox Disproportionation of Aldehydes Lacking α-H with 50% NaOH)
Crossed Cannizzaro: Formaldehyde (HCHO) is EXCLUSIVELY OXIDIZED to Formate (HCOO⁻)
Haloform / Iodoform Diagnostic Test for Methyl Ketones (CH₃CO-) and Methyl Carbinols (CHI₃ ↓)
quickSummary: α-Hydrogens are acidic (pK_a ~20) due to enolate resonance. Aldol requires ≥1 α-H (dil. NaOH) forming α,β-unsaturated carbonyls. Cannizzaro requires 0 α-H (conc. 50% NaOH) yielding 1 mol alcohol + 1 mol carboxylate; in crossed Cannizzaro with HCHO, HCHO is exclusively oxidized to formate. Iodoform test yields yellow CHI₃ ppt with CH₃CO- or CH₃CH(OH)- groups.
summary: Master enolate resonance, aldol and Claisen-Schmidt mechanisms, Cannizzaro disproportionation, and the iodoform diagnostic test.

summaryBox.title: Aldol vs Cannizzaro Criterion
summaryBox.takeaway: HAS α-H (n ≥ 1) ──► Aldol (dil. NaOH). LACKS α-H (n = 0) ──► Cannizzaro (conc. 50% NaOH). In crossed Cannizzaro with HCHO, HCHO oxidizes to formate.

conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Cannizzaro Reaction & Iodoform Test
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CANNIZZARO & IODOFORM REACTIONS:

• Formaldehyde Disproportionation:  2 HCHO + Conc. KOH ──► CH₃OH + HCOOK
• Benzaldehyde Disproportionation: 2 PhCHO + Conc. NaOH ──► PhCH₂OH (Benzyl Alcohol) + PhCOONa
• Crossed Cannizzaro:               PhCHO + HCHO + Conc. NaOH ──► PhCH₂OH + HCOONa (Formate)
• Iodoform Reaction:               CH₃-CO-R + 3I₂ + 4NaOH ──► CHI₃ ↓ (Yellow Ppt) + R-COONa
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Cannizzaro Reaction**: Aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-H ($	ext{HCHO, PhCHO, } (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-CHO}$) disproportionate into alcohol and carboxylate salt.
- **Crossed Cannizzaro**: Formaldehyde is oxidized exclusively to formate because hydride transfer from the formal adduct is fastest.
- **Iodoform Test**: Methyl ketones ($	ext{CH}_3\text{CO-}$) and secondary methyl carbinols ($	ext{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$) yield yellow $	ext{CHI}_3 \downarrow$.

quickRevision: Aldol requires ≥1 α-hydrogen with dilute base.
Cannizzaro requires 0 α-hydrogens with concentrated (50%) base.
In crossed Cannizzaro with HCHO, HCHO is exclusively oxidized to formate.
Iodoform test yields yellow CHI₃ ppt with CH₃CO- or CH₃CH(OH)- groups.
